A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SG/EMA research, with matching authors, title, experiments, and underlying analysis. The complete main texts, four figures, equations, and proof appendices are readable and can be matched across reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: V2 reports original video-classification experiments in Section 2.3 and synthetic simulations in Section 3.3, including training curves and outcomes from 10,000 randomized trials.

after.justification: V3 retains these original video experiments and synthetic simulations in Sections 3.3 and 4.3, with results in Figures 2–4.

M1.justification: The SG and EMA update rules, objectives, and encoder/predictor procedures are unchanged. V3's new final-linear-layer requirement qualifies a theorem; it does not establish a change to the implemented models.

E1.justification: Both versions train video representations on Kinetics710 and SSv2, evaluate classification on K400 and SSv2, and simulate scalar-input linear systems. The new distribution perturbations are proof constructions, not additional evaluated scenarios.

E2.justification: SG and EMA remain the evaluated alternatives in the corresponding video and synthetic experiments. No comparator is added or removed; the cited V-JEPA reference results and discussion of other SSL methods are retained.

E3.justification: The reported protocols retain 300,000 video-training iterations, batch size 1024, learning rate 0.0001, weight decay 0.1, and the same EMA schedule and classification evaluation. Synthetic dimensions, time steps, parameter settings, and initialization procedures also match.

E4.justification: The loss and parameter-increment diagnostics in Figure 2 and the collapse trajectories and objective-value analyses in Figures 3–4 are retained. The appendices add mathematical arguments, not new ablations, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies.

E5.justification: Both versions report 10,000 randomized synthetic trials with the same parameter and initialization distributions. Neither changes run-count reporting or adds seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The plotted results in Figures 2–4 are unchanged. Both versions report outer-circle convergence in 92.8% of EMA trials and 82.0% of SG trials, with the remaining trials converging to the origin. No empirical result entries are added or revised.

T1.justification: V3 substantially expands the proofs of v2 Propositions 2.1–2.2, now 3.1–3.2, with explicit distribution-perturbation arguments and new Proposition 6.1 establishing a nonvanishing Jacobian product. Proposition 3.2 adds smoothness, nonzero-network, and final-linear-layer assumptions. New Proposition 4.7 and Lemma 6.2 address full-rank equilibrium existence under nearby data distributions and sufficiently small regularization using fixed-point and implicit-function arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract, six listed contributions, and conclusion retain the same headline claims about non-optimization, generic collapse avoidance, equilibrium characterization and stability, and empirical behavior. The added technical results support these claims without recasting the headline contribution list.

C2.justification: V3 clarifies applicability through the explicit architectural assumptions in Proposition 3.2 and explains genericity through arbitrarily small distribution perturbations. The interpretations of video performance, observed convergence, and limits on generalizing to other downstream tasks remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Both versions provide the same V-JEPA code-access statement, experimental hyperparameters, synthetic parameter ranges, and initialization information. V3 adds no implementation release, hardware specifications, runtime measurements, or new reproduction instructions.

R1.justification: V3 adds Baldi and Hornik (1989) to relate the limiting matrix identity to deep linear networks, and Hirsch et al. (2013) to support its discussion of genericity. The existing SSL literature and principal novelty positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The opening is substantially reorganized: expanded background and contributions now precede related work and a standalone Problem Setting section, formerly Section 1.1. Introductory and related-work paragraphs are rewritten, a main-text proof sketch is added, and notation is reorganized. Publication headers and acknowledgment placement also change.

P2.justification: All four figures retain their graphical content, but Figures 1, 3, and 4 move, Figure 1's caption gains an equation reference, and surrounding spacing and reference layout change. No new or redesigned figure or table is introduced.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the central non-integrability claim better supported and easier to assess by adding explicit assumptions, a perturbation argument, and a nonvanishing lemma to v2's informal data-dependence reasoning. The reorganized introduction also improves readability. However, the new equilibrium-existence proof contains an algebraic inconsistency: Eq. (42) uses lambda^2 I where normalization of Eq. (6) requires lambda^2 R^{-2}. This limits the theoretical improvement that can be credited as written.
